name: app.json
summary: Obsidian workspace application configuration file storing core UI, editor, and behavioral preferences.
purpose: Persists user-specific application settings for the Obsidian knowledge base client, ensuring consistent behavior, appearance, and editing experience across sessions and synchronized devices.
responsibilities: Store editor preferences such as auto-pairing, live preview, and line length
Persist UI state flags including theme mode, sidebar visibility, and tab behavior
Define default file system behaviors like new note location and attachment folder paths
Serialize application-level feature toggles for consumption by the Obsidian runtime
inputs: User settings changes via the Obsidian Settings UI
Default application schema shipped with Obsidian updates
outputs: Parsed configuration object consumed by the Obsidian client runtime
Serialized JSON state written to disk for persistence across restarts
architecture_notes: Acts as a simple key-value persistence layer using JSON serialization within the workspace metadata boundary. Follows a convention-over-configuration pattern with internal fallback defaults. Coexists with sibling workspace state files (workspace.json, appearance.json, hotkeys.json) to separate concerns. Should be treated as mutable user state rather than infrastructure; include in backups but evaluate whether to version-control based on team synchronization needs.
improvements: Introduce a JSON schema or validation layer to prevent runtime errors from manual edits or sync conflicts
Split into environment-specific overlays (e.g., local-only vs. vault-shared settings) to reduce merge noise
Document setting keys explicitly to improve discoverability for vault administrators and plugin developers
Implement automated migration logic for backward compatibility when Obsidian versions introduce breaking setting changes
